chunks: And whatever is in it from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id Al-Hamadani, I have narrated it from Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq Al-Talqani - may Allah be pleased with him - from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id Al-Hamadani Al-Kufi, the freed slave of Banu Hashim.

key_terms.أَحْمَدَ بْنِ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ سَعِيدٍ الْ: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id Al-Hamadani (a specific narrator)
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him (a honorific for companions or narrators)
key_terms.مَوْلَى بَنِي هَاشِمٍ: Freed slave of Banu Hashim (a genealogical/status descriptor)
key_terms.مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ بْنِ إِسْحَا: Muhammad ibn Ibrahim ibn Ishaq Al-Talqani (the transmitter)

ai.seo_question: Who is the narrator Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'id Al-Hamadani and how was his hadith transmitted?
ai.summary: This passage exemplifies the rigorous chain-of-transmission (isnad) methodology central to Shia hadith scholarship, specifically within Shaykh al-Saduq's *Man La Yahduruhu al-Faqih*. By explicitly linking the narrator Ahmad ibn Muhammad to the Banu Hashim lineage, the text underscores the social and tribal prestige often associated with reliable transmitters in the Kufan scholarly milieu.
